 MISSOULA, Mont. — Two youth-oriented vehicles have been recalled because of crash hazards that could cause serious injuries or death, according to the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission.
 U.S. Titan is recalling about 117 X-Pro Eagle youth all-terrain vehicles because a speed-adjusting module can allow the ATVs to exceed the maximum speed permitted for vehicles intended for children ages 6 and older.
 The gas-powered, 110cc ATVs were sold online at Walmart.com, Powersportsmax.com, Xprousa.com, Amazon.com and eBay from July through September 2025 for $680 to $980.
 Consumers should stop using the speed-adjusting module and contact X-Pro for a $100 refund. The ATV can still be used without the module. Customers will be asked to return the module using a prepaid shipping label.
 Sanven Technology is recalling about 1,950 Vevor BMX bicycles because they lack chain guards. Loose clothing could become caught in the chain, creating a risk of serious injury or death.
 The recall involves black 20- and 24-inch bicycles, models SS24001 and SS24002, sold at Vevor stores nationwide and online at Vevor.com from October 2024 through April 2026 for $152 to $188.
 Consumers should stop using the bicycles and contact Sanven Technology for a free repair kit that includes a chain guard and installation instructions.
 No incidents or injuries have been reported in connection with either recall.
